newsitem.title: GERMANY: German BME/Reuters July PMI adj. 55.32 vs 56.83.
newsitem.headline: German BME/Reuters July PMI adj. 55.32 vs 56.83.

text.p: The BME/Reuters German Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to a seasonally-adjusted 55.32 in July from 56.83 in June, research group NTC Publications Ltd said in a statement released on
On an unadjusted basis it fell to 54.75 from 55.32.
The index, available exclusively on Reuters systems, signalled an expansion of German manufacturing activitiy for the eleventh consecutive month in July.

"A modest decline in the index suggests a slight weakening in the pace of growth for the second month running, but the index nevertheless remained significantly higher than the 50.0 no change level and therefore continues to signal strong growth," NTC said in a statement.
The index pointed to strong, albeit slower growth in the manufacturing sector, with export demand rising because of the weak mark while the pace of growth in domestic demand slowed, NTC said.

The INDEX is based on a survey of 350 companies carried out exclusively for Reuters by research group NTC Publications Ltd in cooperation with the BME German Association for Materials Management, purchasing and Logistics. NTC provided the following data:

NOTE - The PMI is modelled on the closely watched U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) INDEX. A reading below 50 percent indicates that the manufacturing economy is generally declining, while a level above 50 percent shows it generally expanding. The more it deviates from 50, the greater the improvement or decline in the current month. Copyright in the BME/Reuters Purchasing Managers' INDEX is owned by Reuters Limited.
